title: Can an LLM explain its own tabular predictions?
pitch: QLoRA fine-tuned LLMs that classify table rows, then tested whether their explanations are faithful.
did: Serialized rows from the Adult, Wine, CCPP and Student datasets into text and fine-tuned an LLM with QLoRA to predict from them.
Compared three explanation methods for faithfulness and agreement: SHAP, AttnLRP and the model's own self-explanations.
Scored each prediction by full-label log-probability, because the first token is shared between labels, and used a permutation SHAP estimator that works on string columns.
Kept classical baselines (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost) next to the LLM, including a student-grade prediction task.
note: Code is in a private repository.

title: AI due diligence for crypto funds
pitch: A RAG platform that turns crypto-project documents into investor-ready due-diligence answers and reports.
role: Built the retrieval pipeline end to end on my branch.
did: Collected data from the CoinGecko and Scorechain APIs and extracted text from PDFs.
Wrote the NLP cleaning, smart chunking and embedding steps, and the FAISS vector store.
Built the RAG pipeline with hyperparameter tuning, question extraction and a knowledge graph.
Added a first chatbot interface with multi-file upload.

title: HireMind: interview simulation and cheating detection
pitch: An automated candidate-screening agent that runs mock interviews and flags suspicious behaviour.
role: Built the interview simulator, cheating detector, avatar generator and demo on my branch.
did: Cheating detector: flags AI-written answers (perplexity check), unusual answer timing, several voices (audio fingerprinting) and gaze away from the camera.
Interview simulator service (FastAPI): offline speech-to-text, emotion, prosody and stress analysis, answer evaluation and a question bank.
Avatar generator that reads a CV and creates an avatar with Stable Diffusion.
Streamlit demo of the whole flow.

title: Segmenting a bank's company portfolio
pitch: A pipeline that groups companies by financial profile and flags the unusual ones, for credit analysis.
did: Turned each financial ratio into a 0–9 decile score. Missing values count as the worst score when a higher ratio is better, and the best score when lower is better.
Ran 8 anomaly detectors (Isolation Forest, LOF, KNN, an autoencoder, One-Class SVM, HBOS, COPOD and IQR). A company is flagged only when at least 5 agree.
Clustered with a Bayesian Gaussian mixture, which found 4 groups on its own and scored better than K-Medoids and hierarchical clustering.
Built a similarity search that finds a company's closest statistical twins.
note: Confidential bank data: the method is described, the code and data are not published.

title: Churn prediction with a full MLOps pipeline
pitch: A churn model shipped with CI, containers and experiment tracking, not just a notebook.
did: Trained and tuned a churn classifier (SVM grid over C, kernel and gamma) and tracked every run in MLflow.
Served the model with a FastAPI app and packaged it with Docker.
Automated install, code checks, training and tests with a Makefile and a Jenkins pipeline.
note: Code is in a private repository.

title: SAS to Python migration tooling
pitch: Tools that read legacy SAS programs and extract which tables and libraries each one uses.
did: Parsed hundreds of SAS programs, stripping comments and finding permanent libraries through their LIBNAME statements.
Extracted table-level reads and writes into Excel reports to plan the migration to Viya.
note: Parsing scripts and project code are public; no client data is described.

title: What drives student exam scores? A nonparametric study in R
pitch: A CRISP-DM statistical study choosing methods from normality tests instead of assuming them.
did: Cleaned the data with IQR outlier treatment and KNN imputation (k=5).
Tested normality (Jarque-Bera, Q-Q plots), found most variables non-normal, and switched to Spearman correlation, Kruskal-Wallis and Dunn's post-hoc tests.
Found attendance (rho = 0.69) and hours studied (rho = 0.49) the strongest correlates of exam score, while gender and school type were not significant.
